kind.seat: chat with one person from a form

doc.chat: the chat the export comes from (below) — information only: the import always goes into the chat open in the app
doc.me: who exported and what they can do in this chat (below) — information only
doc.exportedAt: the moment of the export (ISO 8601, UTC) — information only
doc.range: what the export covers (below) — information only
doc.topics: the chat's topics — all of them, closed ones too (below: Topic)
doc.messages: messages, oldest first (below: Message from the export, New message)
doc.linked: tasks and appointments created from this chat's messages (below) — read only, the import skips them

chat.id: the chat's identifier; different from the open chat's — a document from another chat: the import skips its messages and creates its topics here as new
chat.title: the chat's name, as in its header

me.name: how this person's message is signed: “First Last”, and when writing through a role — “First Last (Role)”; their messages have "mine": true
me.writes: true — writes in this chat: the import can add their new messages and topics
me.moderates: true — leads the chat: pins, sorts other people's messages too, changes any topic

range.from: since when (ISO 8601; null — from the start of the chat)
range.to: until when (the moment of the export)
range.topic: only messages of this topic ("@key" from "topics") or null — all
range.limited: true — the export reached the limit of {maxExport} messages; older ones from this period are not in it

topic.id: the topic's identifier from the export — with it the import changes THIS topic; without it, it creates a new one (and when a topic with this name already exists, uses the existing one)
topic.key: a short name for references in this document (letters, digits, - and _): a message points to the topic with "topic": "@key"; the export makes it from the name
topic.title: the topic's name (required for a new one, up to {maxTitle} characters); different from the chat's for a topic with "id" — a rename
topic.closed: true — the topic is closed (tucked under “Closed”), false — open; a change closes it or opens it again
topic.createdAt: when it was created — information only
topic.messages: how many messages it has — information only
topic.tasks: how many tasks came from it — information only
topic.appointments: how many appointments came from it — information only

message.id: the message's identifier — with it the import only sorts ("topic", "pinned", "starred"); content, sender and time always stay as they are
message.author: who wrote it — as in the chat: “First Last”, and through a role “First Last (Role)”
message.mine: true — written by the person from "me"
message.link: true — written by a person from a link (without an account)
message.topic: topic: "@key" from "topics" (or the topic's "id"); missing in the export — no topic. In the import, different from the chat — a move (null — out of the topics), missing — no change; moved by the message's author or a leader (one to one and in Notes anyone who writes)
message.replyTo: "id" of the message it replies to
message.attachments: attachments — description only; the files are not in the JSON
message.imported: true — came from a JSON import (marked “From an import” in the chat)
message.edited: when it was last corrected (the edit history is in the chat)
message.deleted: when it was deleted — the content is gone
message.deletedBy: "author" — deleted by its author, "moderator" — by a leader
message.blocked: true — blocked after a report; there is no content
message.unreadable: true — cannot be read in this browser (the key of this epoch of the chat is missing)
message.reactions: reactions — information only (the import doesn't change them)
message.reactions_count: how many people reacted this way
message.pinned: true — pinned for everyone; in the import a change pins or unpins (false) — leaders only
message.starred: true — in the “Saved messages” of the person from "me" (only they see them); in the import a change saves or removes from saved (false)

new.text: content (required; at most {maxText} bytes of UTF-8, counting line breaks and quotation marks twice — a few thousand characters)
new.topic: topic: "@key" from "topics" (also of a new topic from this document) or the "id" of an existing one; missing or null — no topic
new.replyTo: "id" of the message in this chat this replies to — the import takes the quote from that message, never from the document
new.sendAt: schedule sending (ISO 8601 with a time zone, e.g. "2026-12-01T09:00:00+01:00"; from {minMinutes} minutes up to a year ahead) — waits in “Scheduled”, where it can be sent at once or cancelled; without "sendAt" it goes out at once
new.silent: true — without sound: the notification wakes no one

linked.kind: "task" — a task, "appointment" — an appointment in the calendar
linked.title: title
linked.message: "id" of the message the task came from
linked.at: task: the nearest (or last) due time; appointment: the start (ISO 8601)

readOnly: You can only read this chat — the import (topics, sorting, new messages) is for those who write in it. The export works as always.

plan.notDoc: This is not a chat document — one JSON object was expected.

topic.badKey: {where}: "key" may only contain letters, digits, - and _ (up to 40 characters) — references to it won't work.
topic.twice: {where}: the same topic (“{title}”) a second time — skipped.
topic.mayNotChange: {where} (“{title}”): the name is changed and the topic closed by whoever created it or a leader of the chat — skipped.
topic.noIdSkipped: {where}: there is no topic with this "id" in this chat — skipped.
topic.noIdNew: {where}: there is no topic with this "id" in this chat — treated as new.
topic.inNotes: {where} (“{title}”): there are no topics in Notes — skipped.
topic.notWriter: {where} (“{title}”): a topic is created by someone who writes in this chat — skipped.
topic.tooMany: {where} (“{title}”): at most {max} new topics in one import — skipped.
topic.keyTwice: {where}: key "{key}" a second time — "@{key}" points to the first topic with this key.

ref.noKey: {where}: there is no topic with the key "{key}" in "topics" — {instead}.
ref.noTopic: {where}: there is no topic “{title}” in this chat — {instead}.

msg.twice: {where}: the same message a second time — skipped.
msg.older: {where}: older than the loaded messages of this chat (at most {max}) — skipped.
msg.noId: {where}: there is no message with this "id" in this chat — skipped (the import doesn't insert other people's messages).
msg.differs: {label}: {keys} — different from the chat. The import doesn't change a message's content, sender or time (you correct your own in the chat: “Edit”); skipped.
msg.reactions: {label}: the import doesn't change reactions — add yours in the chat.
msg.mayNotFile: {label}: it is moved to a topic by its author or a leader of the chat — it stays where it was.
msg.pinModerator: {label}: pinning and unpinning is done by a leader of the chat — skipped.
msg.goneNoPin: {label}: deleted or unreadable — it cannot be pinned.
msg.goneNoStar: {label}: deleted or unreadable — it cannot be saved.

new.gone: {label}: this describes a deleted or unreadable message, without "id" — skipped.
new.at: {label}: has "at" — the import doesn't write backwards, a message from an import never pretends to be old. Remove "at" (it goes out at once) or give "sendAt" (it schedules it); skipped.
new.author: {label}: "author" is “{author}” — the import writes only as you ({me}), never in someone else's name; skipped.
new.files: {label}: files are not in the JSON — attach them in the chat; the message goes without them.
new.quote: {label}: "quote" skipped — the import takes the quote from the message in "replyTo".
new.ignored: {label}: "{key}" is skipped in a new message.
new.tooLong: {label}: too long ({size} bytes, at most {max}) — split it into several; skipped.
new.sendAtBad: {label}: "sendAt" is not an ISO 8601 date (e.g. "2026-12-01T09:00:00+01:00") — skipped.
new.sendAtSoon: {label}: "sendAt" ({when}) is in the past or too close — you can schedule from {min} minutes ahead; without "sendAt" it goes out at once. Skipped.
new.sendAtFar: {label}: "sendAt" more than a year ahead — skipped.
new.replyMissing: {label}: "replyTo" doesn't point to a loaded message of this chat — it goes without a quote.
new.replyGone: {label}: the message from "replyTo" is deleted or unreadable — it goes without a quote.
new.dupSent: {label}: your message with this content is already in the chat — skipped, so that it isn't there twice.
new.dupWaiting: {label}: the same message is already waiting in “Scheduled” — skipped, so that it isn't there twice.

plan.foreign: The document comes from another chat{source} — its messages won't be moved or copied here{skipped}; its topics will be created here as new.
plan.notWriting: New messages ({count}) skipped — you don't write in this chat.
plan.over: At most {max} new messages in one import — skipped {count}.

line.post: New message as {me}{how}, marked “From an import”: “{text}”
line.nothing: Nothing to change — the document matches the chat.

desc.topic: An entry in "topics". The name is changed and the topic closed by whoever created it or a leader of the chat; there are no topics in Notes. At most {max} new ones in one import.
desc.message: The export describes every message as it is seen in the chat. From messages with "id" the import reads only "topic", "pinned" and "starred" — the rest is for reading: different content, sender or time give a warning and change nothing. Messages not in the document stay.
desc.new: The import sends a message without "id" in this chat as the person importing (their first and last name; when writing through a role — with the role in brackets), marked “From an import”. The order in the document is the order of sending.
desc.newNever: Don't give "author" or "at": a message with another person's "author" or with "at" is skipped. The import skips files ("attachments"), reactions, "pinned", "starred" and "quote" of a new message.
desc.newExample: Example (two new topics and one message in each):
desc.newLater: A message for later, without sound: {"text": "Reminder: …", "sendAt": "2026-12-01T09:00:00+01:00", "silent": true}
desc.linked: An entry in "linked" — a task or appointment someone created from a message of this chat (message menu: “Create task”, “Add to calendar”). Read only: the import skips it.
desc.usage:
- A chat belongs to an area, and access to the chat is access to the area: whoever can read it reads the chat; whoever can write in it writes. So topics and messages from an import are seen by everyone who sees the chat — just like those written by hand.
- The service doesn't read messages: they lie sealed with the area key, and each is signed by the role you write through; the service only checks the signature. The first and last name under a message come from “My data”.
- A new message is unread for others (the bell, “Waiting for you”; the step “Read the messages” loses its tick until they read it) and wakes their phones — Firebase carries only a “check” signal, the content is opened by the phone itself. With "silent": true there is no such signal; it is unread all the same.
- A message with "sendAt" waits sealed in the service; at that time it goes out only if you can still write in this chat — and only then wakes the others.
- A topic is a filter and a place: whoever chooses it sees its messages, and what they write goes into it.
- Tasks and appointments are created from messages in the app (“Create task”, “Add to calendar”) and remember the chat, topic and message; the window “Tasks and appointments from this chat” collects them by topic.
- The import doesn't change who has access to the chat — that is set in the area.

node.usage: How the app uses this data
node.linked: Tasks and appointments from the chat ("linked[]")

sample.topics: two new topics and a message in each
sample.reminder: a reminder for tomorrow morning, without sound

dialog.loadFailed: Could not download this chat's messages.
dialog.loading: Downloading this chat's messages — one moment…
dialog.loadingOlder: Downloading older messages the document refers to — one moment…
dialog.stillLoading: This chat's messages are still downloading — try again in a moment.
dialog.olderLoading: Older messages are still downloading — try again in a moment.
dialog.leadImport: Messages from the chosen period (or topic), topics, tasks and appointments — for the archive or for an AI assistant. The import tidies topics and pins and adds your new messages, marked “From an import”; it never writes in someone else's name or backwards and deletes nothing.
dialog.leadRead: Messages from the chosen period (or topic), topics, tasks and appointments — for the archive or for an AI assistant. You only read in this chat, so there is only the export here.
dialog.note: New messages will go as {name}, marked “From an import”.

lost.one: {count} message was not moved — its topic was not created.
lost.other: {count} messages were not moved — their topic was not created.

notYours.one: {count} message of other people is moved by a leader — it stayed where it was.
notYours.other: {count} messages of other people are moved by a leader — they stayed where they were.

run.notWriting: The new messages did not go out — you don't write in this chat.
run.noTopic: Message {n} of {count} went without a topic — the topic was not created.
run.sendFailed: Message {n} of {count} did not go out: {error}
run.rest: The remaining ones ({left}) didn't either — so as not to change the order.

sent.one: Sent {count} message as {name}, marked “From an import”
sent.other: Sent {count} messages as {name}, marked “From an import”
